pages.title: Project Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to ReactColorPickerDemo — what it is, what it demonstrates, and how the pieces fit together. Links to child pages for setup and architecture details.

page_notes.content: Add emojies and icons to improve the description

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for cloning, installing dependencies, and running the app locally. Covers npm scripts (start, build, test, eject), prerequisites, and the development server.

pages.title: Project Structure
pages.purpose: Explains the repository layout — the public/ and src/ directories, what each file is responsible for, and how the build pipeline connects them.

pages.title: Application Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of how the React component tree is structured and how data flows through the app. Introduces the three components and links to child pages for component details and styling.

pages.title: Component Design
pages.purpose: Deep dive into the three React components defined in App.js: the App root, the stateful ColorPicker class, and the stateless ColorContainer functional component. Covers state initialization, onClick handlers, prop passing, and the unidirectional data-flow pattern.

pages.title: Styling System
pages.purpose: Documents the CSS architecture across index.css and App.css — global resets, layout classes (.App, .App-header, .color-container, .button-container), color-state classes (.color-blue, .color-green, etc.), and the App-logo-spin animation.

pages.title: Build & Runtime Infrastructure
pages.purpose: Overview of the toolchain and runtime support files. Links to child pages covering the dependency manifest, the PWA/public assets, and the service worker.

pages.title: Dependencies & Build Pipeline
pages.purpose: Explains the package.json and package-lock.json in detail — React 17, react-scripts, the Webpack/Babel pipeline, SASS support, tinycolor2 color manipulation, and the four npm lifecycle scripts.

pages.title: Public Assets & PWA Configuration
pages.purpose: Covers the files in the public/ directory: index.html as the HTML shell and DOM mount point, manifest.json for Progressive Web App metadata (icons, display mode, theme/background colors), and favicon.ico multi-resolution icon structure.

pages.title: Service Worker & Offline Support
pages.purpose: Documents registerServiceWorker.js — how it detects localhost vs. production, registers/validates the service worker, handles cache-first serving, and exposes the unregister() escape hatch.

pages.title: Testing
pages.purpose: Describes the testing strategy for the project — the smoke test in App.test.js, the jsdom environment, ReactDOM render/unmount lifecycle validation, and how to run tests with react-scripts.

pages.title: Smoke Test: App Render
pages.purpose: In-depth look at the single test case in App.test.js — its three-phase lifecycle (setup, mount, unmount), what it validates, why ReactDOM.render is used instead of createRoot, and how to extend it with additional assertions.

pages.title: Test Environment & Configuration
pages.purpose: Explains the jsdom test environment flag in package.json, how react-scripts wraps Jest, and guidance for adding component-level or interaction tests in the future.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Definitions of all codebase-specific terms, React concepts, CSS class names, and toolchain abbreviations that an onboarding engineer needs to know, each with code pointers.
